compiled_state.description:
## Why this ticket exists

Epic 6202's stories declare infrastructure but their acceptance criteria require only
DECLARATION, not provisioning. Nothing in CI applies `infra/terraform` (`git grep 'terraform apply'`
finds no job; `docs/gerrit-aws-setup.md` records it as a manual operator step). So a story can —
and did — close green while delivering none of the protection it describes.

**This already happened once.** Story S1 (`aa40`) closed on code evidence and green CI. Its
dedicated gate-scratch EBS volume was never created: absent from AWS, absent from Terraform state,
and `rebar/host:gate_scratch_mounted` read 0 on every datapoint it ever published. Gates kept
writing to the root filesystem — the exact condition ADR 0112 exists to end.

Story S2 (`9183`) is now in the same position, verified against the landed commit `bbe5d228bd2f`:
its three alarms exist in code and in NO AWS account.

This ticket owns the gap so it stops being rediscovered.

## Outstanding provisioning, as of this filing

**1. S1's gate-scratch volume, attachment, and two alarms.** Operator has approved
`terraform apply`. The plan is `4 to add, 1 to change, 0 to destroy`; the one change updates
`aws_instance.gerrit`'s `user_data`, which per provider v5.100.0 defaults triggers a STOP/START of
the instance — an accepted Gerrit outage. A targeted apply was proven IMPOSSIBLE: `main.tf:88-92`
builds `user_data` via `templatefile` with `gate_scratch_volume_id = aws_ebs_volume.gate_scratch.id`,
so creating the volume changes `user_data` by construction, and `-target` cannot prune a real
dependent.

**2. The on-box mount.** Terraform attaches a RAW block device. It does not format, mount, write
fstab, or create the markers — those come from `user_data.sh`, which is cloud-init and runs
once-per-instance; a stop/start keeps the same instance-id, so it will NOT re-run. Until the mount
happens, `gate_scratch_mounted` stays 0, both gate-scratch alarms sit in ALARM, and the gate guard
stays OFF (the predicate refuses only on declaration-present + proof-absent; with NEITHER marker it
is a deliberate no-op). A validated runbook with per-step ABORT conditions exists, produced by
sandbox validation in a real Linux VM with real losetup/mkfs.xfs/mount.

**3. S2's three alarms** — `rebar-docker-storage-cap-high`, `rebar-docker-buildkit-cache-high`,
`rebar-docker-unaccounted-bytes` — declared at `monitoring_autodeploy.tf:393/432/468`, all
`treat_missing_data = "breaching"` and SNS-wired, all absent from AWS. The same apply covers them.

**4. THE DAEMON RESTART, which no apply covers.** S2's `builder.gc` BuildKit cap is installed but
NOT IN FORCE on a live daemon. `systemctl reload docker` was deliberately removed because SIGHUP
applies a fixed key set excluding `builder.gc` — its zero exit was false evidence. Activation is
now OBSERVED (live daemon start time vs `daemon.json` mtime) and FAILS CLOSED, so the install path
correctly and permanently reports NOT in effect until an operator schedules
`systemctl restart docker` in a quiet window. **Nothing tracks whether that restart has happened.**
Until it does, the 5 GiB BuildKit share is uncapped, with `rebar-docker-buildkit-cache-high` as the
only backstop — and that alarm is itself unprovisioned per item 3.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 - The gate-scratch volume exists in AWS and in Terraform state, and is attached.
      Evidence: `describe-volumes` shows it attached to the instance.
- [ ] AC2 - It is formatted, mounted at the configured mount point, and BOTH markers exist with the
      proof marker verifiably ON THE VOLUME (it disappears on unmount and returns on remount).
      `rebar/host:gate_scratch_mounted` publishes **1**.
- [ ] AC3 - `/var/gerrit` is verified mounted after the instance cycle. Nothing in `user_data.sh`
      asserts this (see `unamused-cloudy-junebug`), so a silently-skipped `nofail` mount would leave
      Gerrit on the root filesystem undetected. Gerrit responding is NOT evidence — it responds
      either way.
- [ ] AC4 - All five alarms (2 gate-scratch + 3 docker-storage) exist in AWS with
      `treat_missing_data = "breaching"` and SNS wiring, and their states are recorded. Expect the
      gate-scratch pair to fire immediately before AC2 completes; that is the alarm working.
- [ ] AC5 - `systemctl restart docker` has been performed in a quiet window and
      `docker-storage-cap.sh --install` subsequently reports the policy IN EFFECT. Until this,
      the BuildKit cap is not in force.
- [ ] AC6 - A CHECK exists that distinguishes "declared in Terraform" from "provisioned in AWS",
      so the S1/S2 shape cannot recur silently. Note the Terraform Drift workflow is the natural
      home, but it is itself defective — it runs `fmt -check` before `plan` and was blind for two
      days (`chiselled-glandulous-fantail`). Whatever is built must not depend on that being fixed
      first, or it inherits the same blindness.

## Non-goals

Not changing any story's ACs retroactively. Not applying Terraform outside operator approval.
